item.content:encoded:
"… resulted in the selection of a opposite-gendered Phascolarctos cinereus from its native habitat in Northeastern Australia."

Koala's aren't native to only northeastern Australia. Unless this sentence was more of a "this individual koala's native habitat was northeastern Australia, so that's were it came from".

Nitpicking aside, I was thinking about that koala being returned to the exact spot that it came from, and I realised that if it was in a tree (which it probably was), there was a decent chance of the branch it was on moving enough that the koala was unable to grab it. Mental image of a koala falling out of a tree aside, this would be interesting to explore - a human in a bus/train/car/boat/elevator/plane… basically anything moving. Could make an interesting addendum.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I rather like the entry, but there seem to be some discrepancies when SCP-435 comes into things. For one, 435-2 is the part that enters an active state when 435-1 is not illuminated.

Second, from 435's entry:

Any active state lasting longer than 90 seconds constitutes a potential XK-class end-of-the-world scenario and requires the initiation of Contingency 435-XK-Alpha.

So 435-2 could apparently end the world after 90 seconds of activity. To me, that means three minutes for it to calm down or come to "rest" seems too long.

Then, as someone else already mentioned, 435 and 286 can't have the same composition based on massively conflicting info in the two entries. 435-1 is apparently 99% iron, while 286 is iron, nickel, and something else. And from what we know about 435-2 (which isn't much since it's somewhat dimensionally shifted), there's no way to tell if it shares composition with 286.

I really like this one (286), but those are a few sorta glaring issues with it I wanted to point out.

During a Sigma state, SCP-286-1 and SCP-286-2 will show no reaction to any external stimuli that does not physically interfere with SCP-286-1, SCP-286-2 and their interaction with the game. If something disrupts an ongoing game then either SCP-286-1 or SCP-286-2 will stand and vocalize a statement that most commonly translates as “forfeit,” less commonly as “draw.” This event will also conclude a Sigma state.

Preventing the opposition from reaching the table counts as a disruption. This was the whole trigger for the incident that got this thing reclassed as euclid.

item.title: Ok some edits. . .
item.content:encoded:
Consensus was that referring to Fukishima, even as obliquely as I did, was a problem. So I ditched it (or really just redacted what happened until it could be anything). At the same time, since I still wanted to end with Keter-level shenanigans with an object we thought was safe, I un-redacted the references to SCP-435.

I revised the description to make the Sigma/SCP-286-1/SCP-286-2 relationships clearer, and make the whole section flow a little better. I also cut out some deadwood that wasn't adding to the article.

item.content:encoded:
I was initially somewhat confused about the -1 & -2 & Sigma event thing, since it made it sound like there could only be EITHER a -1 or a -2 in existence, but not both. You clarified it significantly later, but it was still unnecessarily confusing.

Instead of saying that the -1 pieces reflect 75% more light than hits them, you might want to reword that to say that they emit light, at a rate of approximately ~75% greater than what hits them.

And please clarify what you mean by "higher order animals". I'm still unclear as to exactly what that category encompasses, and I suspect that a lot of the species don't have a vocal setup that would allow for even an approximately of human speech. If you mean higher-order simians, it would be better to say that.

Overall, I like it, but I would like to see the above concerns addressed.
